title: Reduced dominant closure and its functorial properties
statement:
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme (one admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings) [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. For a finite-type $S$-scheme $X$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $X_{\mathrm{md}}\hookrightarrow X$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme on the closure of the union of the fibres over the generic points of the irreducible components of $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme, def-weil-irreducible-components]. This is the reduced union of the irreducible components of $X$ whose generic points map to generic points of $S$. The assignment $X\mapsto X_{\mathrm{md}}$ is functorial. If $T$ is reduced, finite type over $S$, and every generic point of $T$ maps to a generic point of $S$, composition with $X_{\mathrm{md}}\hookrightarrow X$ induces a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_S(T,X_{\mathrm{md}})\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_S(T,X).$$
For every generic point $s$ of $S$, $(X_{\mathrm{md}})_s\simeq(X_s)_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-reduced-scheme]. If $f:X\to Y$ is an etale morphism between finite-type $S$-schemes [def-weil-etale-morphism], the canonical map $X_{\mathrm{md}}\to X\times_Y Y_{\mathrm{md}}$ is an isomorphism. If $f$ is proper and surjective [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism], its induced map $X_{\mathrm{md}}\to Y_{\mathrm{md}}$ is proper and surjective.

source.place: Expose II 1.2.5 (coreflection and dominant components), 1.2.8 (proper surjections); the etale comparison follows from flat generization (1.1.3, 1.1.5) and preservation of reduced schemes under etale maps. Printed pp. 23--26.

proof.text: Write $p:X\to S$, let $G$ be the set of generic points of components of $S$, and put $A_X=p^{-1}(G)$. The fibre description [def-pc-scheme-fibre] identifies this set with the union of the generic fibres in the statement. The scheme $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], hence has finitely many components by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components]. By [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover, lem-sc-scheme-sober], every point lies in a component with a generic point. A component generic point $s$ of $S$ has no strict generalization: the closure of any generalization is irreducible, contains the component $\overline{\{s\}}$, hence equals it by maximality, and sobriety gives equality of the points. If $x\in A_X$ and $\xi$ is the generic point of any component containing $x$, continuity gives that $p(\xi)$ generalizes $p(x)\in G$, so $p(\xi)=p(x)$. Thus $A_X$ is contained in the union $C_X$ of components whose generic points map into $G$. Conversely each such generic point belongs to $A_X$, and its entire component lies in $\overline{A_X}$. The finite union $C_X$ is closed, so $\overline{A_X}=C_X$.

Give $C_X$ its reduced induced closed structure using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]; call the inclusion $i_X:X_{\mathrm{md}}\hookrightarrow X$. It is reduced and has exactly the required support. The components of this finite union are exactly the selected components of $X$: every irreducible subset of a finite union of closed subsets lies in one of them, and distinct components of $X$ cannot contain one another. Thus every component generic point of $X_{\mathrm{md}}$ maps into $G$. The closed immersion $i_X$ is proper, in particular finite type, by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Composing with $p$ gives a finite-type $S$-scheme by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. Consequently $X_{\mathrm{md}}$ belongs to the reduced maximally dominant finite-type subcategory, including when $C_X$ is empty.

Let $T$ have the hypotheses in the Hom assertion, and let $u:T\to X$ be an $S$-morphism. By [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover, lem-sc-scheme-sober], every $t\in T$ is a specialization of a component generic point $\tau$. Its image $u(\tau)$ lies over $G$, hence in $A_X$. Continuity gives $u(t)\in\overline{A_X}=C_X$. Since $T$ is reduced, [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] supplies a factorization $v:T\to X_{\mathrm{md}}$. It is unique: on an affine open of $X$, the inclusion is induced by a surjective ring map, so two lifts have identical ring maps after composing with this surjection and hence identical ring maps; these local equalities glue [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The lift is over $S$ because $i_X$ is over $S$ and $i_Xv=u$. This proves exactly the asserted Hom bijection.

source.place: Expose II 1.2.5, printed p. 25; factorization as in Stacks 0356

proof.text: For an $S$-morphism $f:X\to Y$, apply Step 3 with $T=X_{\mathrm{md}}$, which has the required properties by Step 2, to $fi_X$. This defines $f_{\mathrm{md}}$ uniquely by $i_Yf_{\mathrm{md}}=fi_X$. The identity of $X_{\mathrm{md}}$ satisfies the equation for $f=\mathrm{id}_X$; for $g:Y\to Z$, the composite $g_{\mathrm{md}}f_{\mathrm{md}}$ satisfies the equation for $gf$. Uniqueness gives the identity and composition laws. The same equations give naturality of the Hom bijection in both variables, establishing the stated coreflection.

Fix $s\in G$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], base changing $i_X$ gives a closed immersion $j:(X_{\mathrm{md}})_s\to X_s$. Its image is all of $|X_s|$: Step 1 includes every point over $s$ in $C_X$, and [def-pc-scheme-fibre] identifies the fibre topology with that inverse image. By [lem-pur-reduction-generic-fibre] applied to $X_{\mathrm{md}}\to S$, this fibre is reduced, since $X_{\mathrm{md}}$ already is reduced. The same reduced-induced construction on all of $|X_s|$ is $(X_s)_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. The uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] therefore identifies $j$ canonically with $(X_s)_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow X_s$. This proves the generic-fibre assertion, even if $S$ is nonreduced or has several components.

source.place: Expose II 1.2.6 proof, printed p. 25; Stacks 054Z (lemma-reduction-generic-fibre)

proof.text: Suppose $f:X\to Y$ is etale. It is flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism], so its underlying map is open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]. Since $f$ is over $S$, $A_X=f^{-1}(A_Y)$. We check $f^{-1}(\overline{A_Y})=\overline{f^{-1}(A_Y)}$. Continuity gives the inclusion from right to left. If $f(x)\in\overline{A_Y}$ and $U$ is any open neighbourhood of $x$, the open neighbourhood $f(U)$ of $f(x)$ meets $A_Y$. A point in that intersection has a preimage in $U$, so $U$ meets $f^{-1}(A_Y)$. This proves the reverse inclusion. By Step 1 the result is $f^{-1}(C_Y)=C_X$.

source.place: Expose II 1.2.8 proof (open-immersion case), printed p. 26; same open-map closure argument for an etale map

proof.text: Put $P=X\times_Y Y_{\mathrm{md}}$. Its projection to $Y_{\mathrm{md}}$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]; since $Y_{\mathrm{md}}$ is reduced, $P$ is reduced by [etale-proposition-etale-reduced]. Its projection to $X$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], and its support is $f^{-1}(C_Y)=C_X$ by Step 6. Thus the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] gives a unique isomorphism $X_{\mathrm{md}}\simeq P$ over $X$. The canonical comparison is exactly this isomorphism: its two projections are $i_X$ and $f_{\mathrm{md}}$, whose compatibility is the defining equation in Step 4, and a closed immersion admits at most one lift. This proves the etale comparison for the specified canonical map.

source.place: Expose II 1.2.5 and the open-map argument of 1.2.8; Stacks 02GO and 025O

proof.text: Suppose instead that $f:X\to Y$ is proper and surjective. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], the composite $X_{\mathrm{md}}\to X\to Y$ is proper and $Y_{\mathrm{md}}\to Y$ is proper, hence separated. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated] over $Y$ to conclude that $f_{\mathrm{md}}:X_{\mathrm{md}}\to Y_{\mathrm{md}}$ is proper. Its image is closed by the definition of properness [def-weil-proper-morphism]. For each $s\in G$, the base change $X_s\to Y_s$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. Each point of $Y_s$ therefore lifts to a point of $X_s$, which belongs to $C_X$ by Step 1 and hence is a point of $X_{\mathrm{md}}$. Thus the image of $f_{\mathrm{md}}$ contains every point of $Y_{\mathrm{md}}$ above $G$. These points are dense by Step 1 for $Y$, since $Y_{\mathrm{md}}\to Y$ identifies its space with $C_Y=\overline{A_Y}$. A closed subset containing that dense subset is the whole space. This proves surjectivity as well as properness.

proof_origin.place: Expose II 1.1.1, 1.2.5--1.2.8, printed pp. 23--26; coreflection and proper-image argument expanded, etale comparison proved by the open-map closure argument and reduced pullback.

The item statement is the base statement unchanged. Its étale comparison is stronger than ILO's open-immersion case and is proved by the same open-map closure argument. Steps 1-2 are correct: the closure of p^{-1}(G) equals the finite union C_X of the components over generic points, using Stacks 01T6, 0BA8, 004W and 01IS, and the reduced induced structure comes from 01J3. Step 3 is correct: a reduced T whose generic points lie over G maps into C_X, and the map factors through it by Stacks 0356 (schemes.tex l.2269, checked); uniqueness follows from the surjective ring maps of a closed immersion. Step 4 is genuinely elementary. Step 5 is correct: base change of the closed immersion has full support, (X_md)_s is reduced by the 054Z node (more-morphisms l.6690, which needs no hypotheses), and the uniqueness clause gives (X_s)_red; S may be nonreduced. Steps 6-7 are correct: an étale map is open, so f^{-1}(C_Y)=C_X; P = X x_Y Y_md is reduced because it is étale over a reduced scheme, its projection to X is a closed immersion with support C_X, and uniqueness gives P = X_md with the canonical map. Step 8 matches ILO's proof: f_md is proper (01W3/01W5 and proper-to-separated), its image is closed, and it contains the dense set A_Y. I tested an empty dominant part, S=Spec k[e]/e^2 (X_md=X_red), several base components with vertical components of X, and open-immersion and disjoint-union étale maps. A walk over all 92 dependency nodes finds no cycle and no missing node. A search for duplicates finds none: the citer lem-per-alteration-cover-calculus uses the clauses exactly as stated, and generic-fibre-finiteness-criterion has different content. The delivery cites no SGA source. I accept the 20 tool_uses: all are generic Stacks scheme and topology tools.
